_doc: PLAYBOOK 4.2: every promise (titles, thumbnails, hook questions, chapter loops) must be paid off; reviewer FAILs unpaid entries or gaps > 6 min without a partial payoff.

promises.promise: Title 1: every giant wave ever measured, shown to scale
promises.payoffLine: Taan Fiord 193 · Greenland ~200 · Spirit Lake 265 · Tracy Arm 481 · Lituya Bay 524, on the landmark ladder + bar chart

promises.promise: Title 2: a wave taller than the Empire State Building
promises.payoffLine: Water above the 443 m ESB profile (481 m and 524 m)

promises.promise: Title 3: a 481 m wave hit a fjord full of cruise ships
promises.payoffLine: > 20 vessels a day in summer, none in Tracy Arm that morning; cruise lines changed routes

promises.promise: Thumbnail 1: 481 m line on the real slope
promises.payoffLine: Trimline photo with the 481 m mark

promises.promise: Hook: how can water rise higher than a skyscraper?
promises.payoffLine: Mountain falls into a narrow fjord → splash wave → run-up climbs the opposite slope

promises.promise: Hook: was it the tallest wave ever measured?
promises.payoffLine: No — second; Lituya Bay 1958 is the record

promises.promise: Hook: could it happen again with a ship in the way?
promises.payoffLine: Yes, more slopes as glaciers retreat; Barry Arm is moving now; monitoring needed

promises.promise: Loop: why don't ocean tsunamis get this tall?
promises.payoffLine: Ocean tsunamis are wide and low (Japan 2011: 40.5 m)

promises.promise: Loop: which wave holds the record?
